name: XLM-R Multilingual Transformer Text Classification Pipeline Template
summary: Reusable base CDG for Jigsaw multilingual toxic comment classification, multilingual toxicity, low-resource sentiment, Amazon-style multilingual product classification, cross-lingual product taxonomy, and high-cardinality multilingual text classification competitions that combine language-aware cleaning, XLM-RoBERTa-Large or multilingual transformer encoders, language-specific fine-tuning/adapters, taxonomy or label embeddings, intermediate-task transfer, cross-lingual projection/alignment, back-translation, cross-lingual pseudo-labeling, multi-sample dropout, layer-wise learning-rate decay, class-balanced or macro-F1 weighted losses, and calibration.
dejargonized_summary: Clean text from multiple languages, encode it with a multilingual transformer such as XLM-RoBERTa-Large, adapt the model with language or task adapters, optionally align languages or add taxonomy embeddings, create pseudo-labels across languages, train with a metric-aware loss, and calibrate predictions.

inputs.name: multilingual_text
inputs.constraints: Text, labels, language IDs, optional taxonomy or hierarchy metadata.

outputs.name: text_class_predictions
outputs.constraints: Class labels, probabilities, or ranked taxonomy predictions formatted for the benchmark metric.

use_when: The task predicts labels from text in multiple languages, low-resource languages, translated data, multilingual toxicity comments, product titles/descriptions, or product/category taxonomies.

Winning techniques include XLM-RoBERTa-Large/XLM-R, language-specific fine-tuning, language adapters, taxonomy embeddings, cross-lingual alignment/projection, cross-lingual pseudo-labeling, back-translation, multi-sample dropout, layer-wise learning-rate decay, intermediate-task transfer, AUC calibration, or macro-F1 weighted loss.
Language transfer and label imbalance are load-bearing rather than incidental.
do_not_use_when: The task is English-only toxic comment classification with no cross-lingual transfer requirement.
The solution is classic handcrafted text-pair matching with no multilingual transformer fine-tuning.
The main output is generated text or an LLM reasoning answer rather than a fixed classification label.
applicability.key_insight: The durable topology is multilingual representation plus cross-lingual adaptation and metric-aware calibration. This differs from English-only toxic-comment CDGs because language transfer, adapter routing, and cross-lingual pseudo-labels are load-bearing.

swappable_stages.multilingual_encoder: Can use XLM-RoBERTa, mBERT, LaBSE, multilingual DeBERTa, or another cross-lingual transformer.
swappable_stages.cross_lingual_adaptation: Can use language adapters, task adapters, taxonomy embeddings, contrastive alignment, intermediate-task transfer, or projection heads.
swappable_stages.pseudo_label_transfer: Can use translated pseudo-labels, teacher-student self-training, confidence filtering, back-translation augmentation, or language-balanced sampling.

applicability.scaling_notes: Cache tokenization by language, balance batches across languages, and evaluate calibration separately for high- and low-resource language groups.
failure_modes: Pseudo-labels can amplify mistakes in low-resource languages if confidence filtering is too loose.
Adapters can overfit language IDs rather than transferable semantics.
Macro-F1 or class-balanced losses can improve rare classes while hurting frequent-class calibration.

planning_constraints.subject: language_split_before_pseudolabeling
planning_constraints.statement: Define language and validation splits before cross-lingual pseudo-label generation or transfer learning.
planning_constraints.rationale: Pseudo-labeling can leak validation distribution or translated duplicates if language boundaries are not fixed first.

planning_constraints.subject: multilingual_encoder_before_alignment
planning_constraints.statement: Tokenize and encode text with a multilingual backbone before applying language adapters, taxonomy embeddings, or cross-lingual projection heads.
planning_constraints.rationale: Cross-lingual alignment operates on shared multilingual representations, not raw strings.

audit.rationale: Added after validation left repeated multilingual classification cases with missing XLM-RoBERTa-Large/XLM-R, language-specific fine-tuning, cross-lingual pseudo-labeling, back-translation, multi-sample dropout, layer-wise learning-rate decay, taxonomy embeddings, cross-lingual projection, intermediate-task transfer, and macro-F1 weighted losses. Semantic comparison found English toxic-comment and bias-aware transformer CDGs too narrow.
audit.dejargonized_summary: This covers classification solutions where cross-lingual transformer transfer and language-aware calibration are the reusable structure.
uncertainty_notes: English-only moderation and fairness tasks should remain on toxic_comment_1st or jigsaw_toxicity_bias_1st unless multilingual transfer is central.

references.title: Sciona 135-CDG expansion validation audit
references.note: Local deterministic and semantic audit of unmatched multilingual transformer patterns.

stages.name: Language-Aware Preprocessing
stages.description: Normalize multilingual comments, product titles, and descriptions, preserve language-specific characters, attach language IDs, map product taxonomies or label hierarchies, and build language-balanced folds.
stages.dejargonized_description: Clean text without erasing language-specific information and record each example's language.

outputs.name: prepared_text
outputs.constraints: Cleaned text with language and label metadata.

preconditions: Text, labels, and language metadata are available or inferable.
guarantees: Language and label metadata are aligned to each text example.

stages.name: Multilingual Encoder
stages.description: Encode text with XLM-RoBERTa-Large/XLM-R, mBERT, LaBSE, multilingual DeBERTa, or another cross-lingual transformer using language-aware tokenization, multi-sample dropout, layer-wise learning-rate decay, and sequence handling.
stages.dejargonized_description: Use a pretrained multilingual language model to represent text from many languages in a shared space.
preconditions: Tokenizer and maximum sequence length are fixed.

stages.name: Cross-Lingual Adaptation
stages.description: Apply language-specific fine-tuning, language adapters, task adapters, taxonomy embeddings, product category embeddings, cross-lingual projection/alignment heads, intermediate-task transfer learning, or contrastive language alignment.
stages.dejargonized_description: Adapt the multilingual model so labels transfer across languages and taxonomies.
preconditions: Adapter or alignment policy is selected.
guarantees: Adapted representations preserve target label semantics.

stages.name: Pseudo-Label Transfer
stages.description: Generate cross-lingual pseudo-labels with confidence filtering, translated teacher-student transfer, back-translation augmentation, language-balanced sampling, or low-resource self-training.
stages.dejargonized_description: Use confident predictions or translations to add training signal in languages with less labeled data.
preconditions: Validation boundaries and confidence thresholds are fixed.
guarantees: Pseudo-label provenance and language coverage are explicit.

stages.name: Metric Calibration
stages.description: Train and calibrate classification heads with AUC-aware toxicity calibration, macro-F1 weighted loss, class-balanced BCE/CE, taxonomy-aware loss, threshold tuning, language-group calibration, or fold ensembling.
stages.dejargonized_description: Convert multilingual model outputs into metric-calibrated class predictions.
preconditions: Metric, labels, and language groups are known.
guarantees: Predictions are calibrated and formatted for submission.
